title: The glue that was thrown away because it stuck to everything
hook: A glue was thrown away because it stuck to everything.
summary: Chemist Harry Coover discovered super glue in 1942 while making gun sights, rejected it for sticking to everything, then rediscovered it in 1951 when it ruined two lab prisms.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica and Smithsonian: Harry Coover found cyanoacrylate in 1942 while seeking clear plastic for gun sights at Eastman Kodak's lab; it was too sticky to use.
Smithsonian/Kodak history: in 1951 Coover and Fred Joyner, testing for jet canopy coatings, found it bonded refractometer prisms; sold as Eastman 910 in 1958.

lines.text: A glue was thrown away because it stuck to everything.
In nineteen forty-two, chemist Harry Coover was trying to make clear gun sights.
lines.caps: In *1942, | chemist Harry *Coover | was making clear *gun sights

lines.text: Instead, his plastic glued everything it touched, so he gave up.
lines.caps: Instead, it *glued | everything it *touched, | so he gave *up

lines.text: Nine years later, he tested it again for jet canopies.
lines.caps: *Nine years later, | he *tested it for | jet *canopies

lines.text: A colleague spread it between two costly lab prisms, and they stuck fast.
lines.caps: A colleague *spread it | between two *prisms, | and they stuck *fast

lines.text: This time Coover saw the point: a glue needing no heat or pressure.
lines.caps: This time *Coover | saw the *point: | no *heat, no pressure

lines.text: In nineteen fifty-eight it went on sale.

post.caption:
Super glue was rejected once because it was too sticky. Then it ruined two lab prisms and became a product.
What useful thing have you found by accident?
